metadata.description: Adds bootstrap 95% CIs to the founder-exit/survival experiment's Cohen's d snapshot-covariate effect sizes and (attempted) placebo percentile, plus a 12-repo manual GitHub identity-resolution spot-check, and reclassifies the three pre-registered success criteria.

covariate_ci_table.method: nonparametric bootstrap, B=10000, resample survivor/nonsurvivor groups independently with replacement at original sizes; Cohen's d recomputed per resample with pooled SD; 95% CI = 2.5th/97.5th percentile of bootstrap distribution

table.note: raw per-repo covariate values are null/absent for all TFDD repos in the experiment artifact (GitHub API metadata fetch returned nothing for stars/forks); not silently fabricated.
raw per-repo covariate values are null/absent for all TFDD repos in the experiment artifact (GitHub API metadata fetch returned nothing for stars/forks); not silently fabricated.

placebo_ci.gap_statement: A proper bootstrap CI on the placebo percentile is NOT reconstructable from method_out.json as saved: the artifact persists only the scalar percentile/p-value, not the raw within-repo null-window draws or the pooled array of null effect-size resamples that produced them. Recomputing these requires re-mining commit history via git/GitHub API for all 30 TFDD repos (method.py's placebo_windows() needs the full FileEvents/commit log per repo, which is not persisted either), which this evaluation artifact deliberately avoids per the 'do not re-execute the method' guidance. This is a concrete, named gap: the next experiment iteration should persist the raw per-repo null_windows list and the pooled null_effect_sizes array (25-200 floats) alongside placebo_results so this CI becomes computable without a rerun.
placebo_ci.point_estimate_caveat: At face value the point estimate (40.0th percentile, p=0.6153846153846154) sits close to the 50th-percentile 'no signal' region. Given only n_null_draws=25 null draws were achieved (vs the pre-registered target of 200, itself already reduced from 1000), the true sampling variance around this percentile is almost certainly large enough to include both 'no signal' (~50th percentile) and a real weak effect (<25th or >75th percentile) -- but this cannot be quantified into an actual interval from the artifact as saved, so the point estimate should NOT be presented as if it settled the question.

identity_spotcheck_results.method_note: Ground truth = the earliest commit reachable from the repo's default branch via the unauthenticated GitHub REST API (no token, no aii-web-tools authenticated calls), located by binary-searching the commits endpoint's Link:rel=last page count at per_page=1. This checks criterion (a) from the plan (founder identity vs actual first-committer) directly; criterion (b) (noreply-alias parsing) is checked opportunistically whenever the earliest commit itself uses a noreply address. Criterion (c) (missed/over merges among non-founder contributors) could not be checked from this endpoint alone since method_out.json does not persist the pipeline's internal alias-merge graph -- flagged as a scope limitation of this spot-check, not silently skipped.
identity_spotcheck_results.serious_finding_note: 1 of 12 decidable repos showed the earliest-commit author not matching the pipeline's founder identity. Whether this would change TF=1/founder-only-TFDD qualification for those events requires manually reading each repo's early commit list beyond the single earliest commit (e.g. a bot/mirror commit, or a legitimate co-founder), which is beyond what this endpoint alone determines -- reported here as a flagged risk, not resolved.

original_success_criteria_verdict.notes: Corpus of 62 curated GitHub repos (dataset artifact dependency was empty at run time, see corpus_stats/notes). 47 passed prefilters, 30 yielded a founder-only TFDD with sufficient pre/post history. Snapshots are QUARTERLY (fallback_plan item 3) with a documented ~1.5mo TFDD-date fuzz. Placebo uses 200-target null draws (reduced from 1000 for CPU budget). DL(a,f) is implemented as the standard Fritz/Avelino definition: count of commits to f by OTHER authors after a's own last commit to f (not independently re-verified against the ICPC 2016 paper text at run time -- documented deviation from testing_plan step 1). REPORTING A NULL/NEGATIVE RESULT: corpus too small or effects do not clear thresholds; per fallback_plan, no fabrication/downsampling was applied.

criteria_reclassification.reason: matched_pairs_results.status='insufficient_group_sizes' (n_high=0, n_low=0); the matching procedure never produced usable high/low-diffusion groups at n=30, so no ratio or CI exists to evaluate for low resolution vs a genuine null.
criteria_reclassification.implication: A future iteration needs a substantially larger founder-only-TFDD corpus (more than 30) before matched-pairs group sizes clear the >=3-per-arm minimum.

criteria_reclassification.criterion: BH-FDR-significant diffusion coefficient exceeding snapshot-covariate coefficient
criteria_reclassification.reason: regression_results.status='insufficient_data_or_no_outcome_variance', n_used=0 (< the 12-observation minimum the pipeline itself requires for the standardized logit); no coefficients or BH-adjusted p-values were ever produced.
criteria_reclassification.implication: Needs a larger corpus with non-null log_stars/log_forks (this run's stars/forks were entirely NULL, see Step 1) and >=12 usable TFDD repos with outcome variance.

criteria_reclassification.criterion: placebo/shuffle check shows weaker effect at randomly relocated windows
criteria_reclassification.reason: point estimate: 40.0th percentile, empirical p=0.6153846153846154, but built from only n_null_draws=25 (target 200, itself reduced from 1000 for CPU budget), and Step 2 of this evaluation could not reconstruct a bootstrap CI from the saved artifact to formally bound this -- the low raw draw count is itself direct evidence the point estimate is underpowered, so we classify conservatively as low-resolution rather than a resolved null.
criteria_reclassification.implication: Persist the raw null-window draws (see Step 2 gap_statement) and restore the target of 200-1000 null draws so a genuine bootstrap CI on the percentile is computable without a full method.py rerun.

success_criteria_reclassification.overall_statement: Two of three pre-registered success criteria (matched-pairs, regression) never ran to completion -- they are UNTESTABLE_AT_SCALE, not TESTED_NULL, because the founder-only-TFDD corpus (n=30) never cleared the pipeline's own minimum group/observation sizes. The third (placebo) did run to completion but only reached 25 of a targeted 200 null draws and this evaluation could not reconstruct a rigorous CI on its percentile from the saved artifact, so it is downgraded to TESTED_LOW_RESOLUTION rather than accepted as a resolved null. None of the three criteria currently supports a confident 'the diffusion signal does not predict survival' conclusion; the honest reading is 'not enough power to tell' for all three, which matches the hypothesis's own self-critique. The five snapshot covariates fare better: three (developers, commits, files) have real per-repo raw values and now bootstrap-CI'd Cohen's d; two (stars, forks) are simply absent from the artifact (GitHub metadata fetch returned null for the entire corpus) and are NOT_COMPUTABLE, not zero.
